question: Are extended warranties worth what dealers and retailers charge for them?
rationale: Car and appliance buyers are pitched extended warranties at checkout with confident claims that they cover whatever breaks and more than pay for themselves over the life of the purchase. Finance channels, a former dealership insider and viral TikTok and YouTube videos push back just as confidently that most buyers never file a claim and spend far more on the contract than they ever recover. Consumer Reports' own reader surveys, an FTC-commissioned economics paper and a legal-aid report that priced dealer markups state by state can decide exactly how often that trade-off actually favors the buyer.
fit: The Commission on Spending already asks what a heat pump or a tariff really costs a household against the confident pitch sold alongside it. Extended warranties are the same question applied to the add-on sold with nearly every car and major appliance purchase: a product priced on a sales floor, defended by the industry that profits from it, and disputed by consumer advocates with the receipts to check it. It continues the channel's focus on real savings versus a confident sales pitch, this time at the point of sale rather than the utility bill.
claims: Dealers make more profit selling the extended warranty than the car itself.
Dealer markups roughly double the actual cost of providing the coverage.
Most buyers who purchase an extended warranty never file a single claim.
Owners typically pay far more for coverage than they recover in repairs.
Independent warranty providers sell the same coverage for much less than dealers.
Warranty salespeople earn bigger commissions the more they mark up the price.
Appliance extended warranties only pay off on expensive, high-failure built-in units.
A manufacturer's warranty already covers most of what an extended warranty duplicates.
Service contracts exclude many of the repairs buyers assume they cover.
Telemarketers selling extended warranties falsely claim to represent the manufacturer.
Financing a warranty into a car loan adds interest on top of the markup.
Reliable car models rarely need the repairs an extended warranty would cover.
